# Reading a unit's magnitude, compiled and run as Go.
#
# testdata/unit_base_field_interpolation.txtar says what the three targets
# generate; this says the Go they generate builds. That is the claim the whole
# class of bug here needs, because every one of them was invisible for exactly
# the same reason: `sngl generate` wrote invalid code to disk and exited 0.
# `("px is " + m.m.Px)` is a string plus a float64, and before the checker
# typed a per-base read as a float, that is what came out.
#
# The assertions are on the magnitudes rather than on the text, so the test
# fails if the arithmetic is wrong as well as if the file does not build. A
# test agent reads a component's own state and not a field of it, which is why
# the reads are copied into scalars by a mount effect.
#
# `int(d)` is in the view but not asserted, and deliberately: a duration's base
# is ms, and `int(d)` is 500 on Kotlin and JavaScript but 500000000 in Go,
# where the value is a time.Duration and converting one yields nanoseconds.
# That divergence is its own bug; asserting either number here would pin one
# target's answer as though it were the language's.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"

unit tick {
    tk
}

component main ui.node {
    var m ui.measurement = 3px
    var t tick = 4tk
    var d time.duration = 500ms
    var widePx = 0.0
    var ticks = 0.0

    effect(@mount {
        widePx = m.px
        ticks = float(t)
    })

    ui.text(value="px is {m.px}")
    ui.text(value="tk is {float(t)}")
    ui.text(value="ms is {int(d)}")
}

func testAPerBaseFieldIsANumber(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.widePx == 3.0)
}

func testASingleBaseUnitConverts(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.ticks == 4.0)
}

ui.window {
    main
}
